issues.issue: Item (i) deducts 'any payments made in respect of premiums on lender paid insurance mortgage loans,' a garbled phrase that names no identifiable category of payment. What is subtracted from scheduled interest is uncertain.

The definition fixes the rate by reference to 'the then applicable highest rate of interest on the Insured Notes' and to a determination 'by the Class A Note Insurer,' neither of which is a defined term or a party in this Agreement. The rate cannot be computed from the instrument as drafted.

The definition makes the Latest Possible Maturity Date a floating date computed from the Mortgage Loan with the latest scheduled maturity, while the Preliminary Statement tables fix it at December 25, 2046 for every Class. The formula and the tabulated date need not produce the same day.

Limb (i) requires an actual liquidation with all expected recoveries received, while limb (ii) deems any loan '180 days or more delinquent' to be a Liquidated Mortgage Loan although nothing has been liquidated. The two limbs give the same defined term two incompatible senses.

'Majority in Interest' is defined in words materially identical to the separately defined 'Majority Holder' (51% of the Percentage Interests of a Class of Regular Certificates), the only difference being singular versus plural Holders. Whether the two terms mean different things where the Agreement uses them separately is left open.

The account is said to be established 'pursuant to 3.07(j) of this agreement,' a citation omitting the word Section and not verifiable against the subsection lettering used for the other Section 3.07 accounts. The establishing provision must be located by inference.

Limb (b) is itself 'the lesser of (a) the product of ... and (b) the aggregate Stated Principal Balance ... minus the OC Floor,' reusing the letters (a) and (b) that already label the outer limbs. The nesting error makes the computation ambiguous on its face.

'Mortgage' is defined as an instrument 'creating a second lien' on the mortgaged estate, yet the Agreement's Loan-to-Value Ratio, Primary Insurance Policy and foreclosure provisions all presuppose that the Trust holds the senior security. Whether the Trust's loans are first or second liens cannot be settled from this definition alone.

Items (5) and (7) require the 'Scheduled Principal Balance' of each Mortgage Loan, a term the Agreement does not define, and item (33) is simply '[reserved].' The content of the schedule on those points is indeterminate.

Mortgaged Property is confined to one- to four-family dwellings and individual condominium units, but the Agreement separately contemplates Cooperative Mortgage Loans secured by Cooperative Shares and a Proprietary Lease rather than by such real property. The definition does not accommodate the cooperative collateral the Agreement elsewhere assumes.

For the Class 1-A-3, Class 2-A-3 and Class 4-A-2 Certificates the Net Rate Cap is reduced by the Certificate Insurer Fee Rate, so the insurer's premium comes out of the insured holders' rate, while Endorsement No. 1 to the Certificate Insurance Policy excludes from Guaranteed Distributions any shortfall 'resulting from application of the Net Rate Cap.' Whether the premium-driven reduction is an insured shortfall or one the holders bear turns on reading the two instruments together.

Net Rate Carryover measures the interest lost to the Net Rate Cap for the Insured Certificates among others, but under Section 4.02 it is payable only out of Net Monthly Excess Cashflow and the Carryover Reserve Fund and is expressly outside the Guaranteed Distributions defined in Endorsement No. 1 to the Policy. Whether holders of Insured Certificates have any enforceable entitlement to it requires reading those provisions together.

'NIMS Insurer' is defined as 'any insurer' guaranteeing notes secured by certain Certificates, with no requirement that one exist, be identified, or give notice, yet the Agreement conditions numerous actions on its consent. Whether a NIMS Insurer exists at any time, and who it is, cannot be determined from the definition.

Recoverability turns on 'the good faith judgment of the applicable Servicer or the Master Servicer,' with no objective standard, evidentiary requirement or review mechanism. Whether an Advance is nonrecoverable is left to an undefined subjective test.

An Officer's Certificate may be signed only by officers of the Depositor or the Master Servicer, although the Agreement elsewhere requires certificates from the Trustee, Trust Administrator and Custodian. The definition's enumeration excludes signatories the Agreement assumes.

Counsel need only be 'reasonably acceptable to the Trustee or the Trust Administrator,' a standard with no criteria and with no indication of which of the two officers' acceptance governs. The qualification is left to be judged after the fact.

The term covers only the Senior and Mezzanine Certificates, yet the Preliminary Statement's Middle REMIC 2 notes size interests by 'the Original Certificate Principal Balance of its Corresponding Class of Certificates' for classes outside that group. The definition does not reach every class that uses it.
